decisions.reason: NL requires 'This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected,' i.e. the sub-machine's default entry must select a named mode. The exact closed-model edge transition:line:39 ([*] -> UnspecifiedInitial) targets a synthetic placeholder state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:35, not any of Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian. The only competing reading (satisfaction via the separate root-level edge into CollisionAvoidanceSystem) addresses a different, already-satisfied contract and is explicitly excluded by the dossier's own strongest_rebuttal analysis, so it is defeated rather than surviving as a rebuttal.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The separate root->CollisionAvoidanceSystem edge (transition:line:45) is satisfied, but that is a distinct entry contract and does not discharge this owner-local obligation.
decisions.violated_obligation: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's owner-local initial edge must select one of Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian upon detection; instead it targets synthetic UnspecifiedInitial.

decisions.reason: NL requires distinguishable frontend/rear-end/pedestrian triggered activation branches. The exact closed model (fcstm_model.events, inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions, exact_source_inventory.transitions) shows only generic Collision_Detected/Brake_Applied/Collision_Avoided events reused identically inside each composite, and no shared-source branch group realizing the three alternatives at all; CollisionAvoidanceSystem's only entry edge is the unconditioned edge to UnspecifiedInitial. The proposed generic-Collision_Detected reading is explicitly noted in the dossier as unsupported by any exact source/model evidence assigning distinct identities, so it is defeated rather than a surviving rebuttal.

decisions.violated_obligation: Three mutually exclusive, separately triggered transitions keyed by the three collision-detection events must exist from the enclosing scope into the corresponding active modes.

decisions.reason: The NL/source inventory (lines 4, 11, 18) shows three separate blocks (Frontend, Pedestrian, RearEnd) each declaring/entering a state named 'Idle', but PlantUML's global state-name resolution semantics collapse these into a single closed-model state (CollisionAvoidanceSystem.Frontend.Idle). This is an established source-to-model naming defect. issues.strongest_rebuttal: One might argue the malformed nested edge is purely a compiler/source-encoding artifact and that Frontend's fully realized Idle/Braking/Clamping structure demonstrates the intended pattern was authored correctly at least once, so the author's intent for RearEnd/Pedestrian is clear even though the edge target resolved out-of-scope; but the exact owner-local edge for those two owners is still malformed and does not reach a valid child in their own scope.
issues.title: RearEnd and Pedestrian composites' owner-local initial edges target an out-of-scope/synthetic placeholder instead of their own operating substates

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text lines defining CollisionAvoidanceSystem's [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial and Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian -> [*] exit guards; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions line:39/line:42; inspection_equivalent_facts.states reachable_from_initial flags for Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian.
issues.expected: The owner scope (CollisionAvoidanceSystem, entered from root) must have an initial/default entry path that activates one of Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian (the collision-avoidance sub-machine) upon detection.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's only outgoing initial pseudostate edge (transition:line:39) targets UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:42 confirms UnspecifiedInitial is the sole reachable descendant); Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian each have local [*]-> edges but none is reachable from CollisionAvoidanceSystem's own entry, per inspection_equivalent_facts.states (reachable_from_initial=false for all three) and verify_facts refuted reachability checks.
issues.reason: The exact owner-local initial pseudostate edge inside CollisionAvoidanceSystem targets only the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial placeholder, never the three named collision-avoidance sub-machines that must activate on detection; this is a scoped S2 initial-edge defect distinct from the local child-initial edges inside Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian each declare a local initial pseudostate edge ([*] -> Idle / InvalidInitialtr_0005 / InvalidInitialtr_0009), which could be read as satisfying an entry obligation scoped to each sub-machine individually rather than the owner-level activation obligation; however the contract's binding_hints scope the entry to the enclosing root/controller reaching the active mode, which fails.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's default/initial entry never reaches any of the three collision-avoidance sub-machines

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers rows for Collision_Detected/Brake_Applied; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE entries; verify_facts.checks event-consumer refuted rows.
issues.expected: Each collision-detection event must be consumed by a reachable transition in the enclosing scope so that detection actually activates the corresponding sub-machine.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers shows Collision_Detected's declared consumer_transition_refs (line:12,15,18) all have empty reachable_consumer_transition_refs; the diagnostics list explicitly flags EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Collision_Detected and Brake_Applied; verify_facts.checks confirms both event-consumer checks as refuted.
issues.reason: The registry has no frozen event-consumer-coverage predicate distinguishing declared vs. reachable consumers, so this precise semantic gap is preserved as a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than dropped or misrouted to S1/S2.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The Collision_Avoided event does have a reachable consumer (UnspecifiedInitial's transition:line:42), which could be argued as generic sub-machine-activation coverage, but that reachable consumer is the synthetic placeholder state, not any of the three named collision-detection consumers, so it does not rebut the unconsumed detection events.
issues.title: Collision_Detected (and Brake_Applied) events have declared consumers but none reachable in the enclosing scope

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text (no Collision_Detected-triggered edge into Frontend from CollisionAvoidanceSystem); inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions complete list (line:36-45) showing no such edge; inspection_equivalent_facts.states Frontend reachable_from_initial=false.
issues.expected: On detection of a possible frontend collision, the enclosing scope (CollisionAvoidanceSystem, entered from root) must transition into the active mode realized by the Frontend collision-avoidance sub-machine.
issues.observed: The complete closed transition inventory contains no edge from CollisionAvoidanceSystem (or its initial pseudostate) into Frontend; CollisionAvoidanceSystem's only initial edge (transition:line:39) targets UnspecifiedInitial, and no event-triggered transition anywhere targets Frontend as an entry.
issues.reason: The contract requires an exact enclosing-scope-to-active-mode transition triggered by frontend-collision detection; the complete transition inventory has no such edge, so this is a complete-inventory absence candidate bound to the existing endpoint state refs.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Frontend does have its own local [*] -> Idle edge (transition:line:11), so an argument could be made that Frontend is 'entered' internally by design once control somehow reaches it; but the complete inventory shows no exact CollisionAvoidanceSystem-to-Frontend edge triggered by a frontend-collision event, so the wrong-target/missing-edge fact stands at the contract's own source/target level.
issues.title: No transition realizes enclosing-scope to Frontend activation on frontend-collision detection

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text CollisionAvoidanceSystem block; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions complete list; NL2 transition_groups ALT-NL2-FRONTEND/REAREND/PEDESTRIAN alternatives with observed_transition_ref=null.
issues.expected: The three collision-detection events must select distinguishable, mutually exclusive activation branches from the enclosing scope into Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian respectively.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's only outgoing initial-scope edge is the unconditional transition:line:39 to UnspecifiedInitial; there is no shared-source transition group with three event-differentiated branches to Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian anywhere in the closed model, so the three alternatives cannot be compared as distinguishable branches because none of them is instantiated as a triggered branch at all.
issues.reason: Guard/trigger disjointness has no frozen predicate and here the underlying activation branch group itself is absent from the closed model, so the precise obligation is preserved as a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than silently satisfied or dropped.
issues.requirement_quote: a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each sub-machine (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian) does have its own internal Collision_Detected-triggered edge (Idle->Braking), so one could argue the three collision types are locally distinguished within their own regions; but the contract's normative locus is the shared activation-selection relation at the enclosing scope, which does not exist in the closed model.
issues.title: The three collision-detection activation alternatives are not realized as distinguishable branches from a shared source

issues.basis: canonical_source_ir.model.concurrent_regions count=0; inspection_equivalent_facts.states reachable_from_initial=false for Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian; verify_facts.checks refuted reachability rows.
issues.expected: The Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian collision-avoidance controls must be capable of simultaneous, concurrent operation within the active mode.
issues.observed: Frontend, RearEnd, and Pedestrian are modeled as sequential sibling composites with no orthogonal/parallel region structure (canonical_source_ir.model.concurrent_regions count=0), and only CollisionAvoidanceSystem's UnspecifiedInitial placeholder branch is reachable from root; Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian are all unreachable per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts, so none of the controls can even individually activate, let alone concurrently.
issues.reason: state_action here expresses a concurrent-capability obligation with no frozen predicate coverage; the exact non-orthogonal, largely-unreachable composite structure is preserved as a predicate-null W1 candidate rather than silently dropped.
issues.requirement_quote: The orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: If a future entry defect (NL-CONTRACT-REF-002) were fixed so all three sibling composites became reachable, they would still execute independently rather than concurrently since the model has no orthogonal-region construct; conversely one could argue the request only needs three independent controls without true UML orthogonality, but the NL explicitly says 'orthogonal regions... allow concurrent activation,' which the model does not realize.
issues.title: Distinct collision-avoidance controls cannot operate concurrently because their owning composites are not orthogonal and are largely unreachable

cardinality_bindings.basis: NL1 quote 'There are three region in this diagram'; NL3 quote 'orthogonal regions of the active mode of collision avoidance'; exact_source_inventory.states rows for CollisionAvoidanceSystem/Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian; canonical_source_ir.model.concurrent_regions count=0.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL1 says 'There are three region in this diagram,' which textually asserts concurrent/parallel region semantics, matching NL3's explicit 'orthogonal regions' language for the same active-mode composite. However, the closed FCSTM and canonical source IR show CollisionAvoidanceSystem containing three ordinary sequential sibling composite states (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian) with no parallel-region separator (canonical_source_ir.model.concurrent_regions count=0), so whether NL intends true UML orthogonal regions (member_domain=concurrent_regions, and a non-empty composite without a separator would count as one implicit region, not three) or simply three named child composites (member_domain=direct_child_states or explicit_named_members counting Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian) cannot be resolved to one primary reading from the supplied NL and source facts alone. I preserve both readings without selecting one as the deterministic frontier reviews the complete inventory.

branches.reason: Behavioral-consequence review of the closed FCSTM shows a root chain llms_emp_feedback_final_0047 -> CollisionAvoidanceSystem -> UnspecifiedInitial reachable, but none of Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian (the three collision-avoidance sub-machines named by NL2) is reachable from the top-level initial entry: CollisionAvoidanceSystem's own [*] edge targets only UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:39/42), never Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian. This makes the required activation-on-detection obligation (NL2 initial_entry contract, its derived event-consumer-coverage contract, and its derived frontend-alternative transition-endpoint contract) all fail on reachable-operational grounds even though local child-initial edges (Frontend [*]->Idle, RearEnd [*]->InvalidInitialtr_0005, Pedestrian [*]->InvalidInitialtr_0009) exist. Deterministic facts confirm: inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Collision_Detected and Brake_Applied; event_consumers rows show reachable_consumer_state_refs=[] for both events; verify_facts refutes reachability for Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian/Idle/Braking/Clamping/InvalidInitialtr_0005/InvalidInitialtr_0009 and refutes event-consumer checks for Collision_Detected and Brake_Applied. The NL2-DISJOINT-1 guard_disjointness contract remains a precise but non-executable claim (no frozen predicate distinguishes the three alternatives; also none of the three alternatives is even instantiated as an owner-level branch in the closed model, since CollisionAvoidanceSystem's outgoing edge is unconditional to UnspecifiedInitial only) -> predicate-null W1. NL3 region-structure/state-action/containment contracts concern the *active mode* structure (Frontend/RearEnd/Pedestrian as orthogonal regions of one active mode); FCSTM instead models them as three separate sibling composites under CollisionAvoidanceSystem with independent local sub-state machines, none reachable, so the orthogonal/concurrent-activation property cannot be exercised behaviorally either. NL1 cardinality is handled via cardinality_bindings only, no candidate. The stable termination contract is not directly present in the plan (no explicit termination contract supplied) so no termination candidate is emitted here, but note CollisionAvoidanceSystem's own exit is guarded by R45RouteToken==14 which is only set by descendant sub-machine completions that are themselves unreachable -- this reinforces the dead-end/coverage findings already captured under NL2 obligations; I do not synthesize a new termination contract since no NL segment states an explicit termination-state role for this locus.
